title: Singi Talav · tools in context
alt: Five labelled groups of stone artefacts with a five-centimetre scale.
caption: Published Figure 3. Panel c is from Layer 4; a and b belong to other layers. Panels d and e came from an eroding quarry edge, so the entire plate must not be assigned the scene's approximately 177,000-year date.

title: Singi Talav · excavated sequence
alt: Excavation sections SGT6 and SGT7 beside age estimates and environmental measurements.
caption: Published Figure 2 preserves the separate layers, age estimates and environmental proxies. Open the full image to read the labels; the timeline highlights one part of this longer sequence.

title: Dhaba · layers and dated samples
alt: Four labelled sediment profiles with luminescence ages and sample locations.
caption: Published Figure 3. Ages refer to sampled sediments and include uncertainties. Cryptotephra at Dhaba 1 lies between samples dated approximately 78,000 and 71,000 years ago.

title: Dhaba · a changing toolkit
alt: Labelled Levallois flakes, cores, ochre and microlithic artefacts with scale bars.
caption: Published Figure 4 combines finds across roughly 80,000–25,000 years. Microblade cores h–i, blades n–o and backed pieces t–u come from Dhaba 3. This is a comparative plate, not a single dated assemblage.

title: Mehtakheri · microblade technology
alt: Drawings of cores and slender blades, specimen labels and a five-centimetre scale.
caption: Published Figure 10. The plate includes excavated specimen J4 and surface-collected XX4. These collection contexts differ; the approximately 45,000-year sediment estimate is not a direct date for every illustrated object.

title: Mehtakheri · the 2009 excavation
alt: Tall excavation section with numbered sediment layers and a field scale.
caption: Published Figure 4 records the 2009 excavation. Layers 18–26 form the artefact-bearing Unit 2; its upper contact is erosional. The photograph's capture year is distinct from the archaeological age.

title: Lahuradewa · regional plant-evidence map
alt: Regional archaeological map; Lahuradewa is numbered 15.
caption: Bates (2022), Figure 1: Lahuradewa is site 15. The map collects sites discussed in the review; it does not show a single contemporary farming network or prove domestication at every location.
credit: Jennifer Bates (2022), Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution

title: Mehrgarh · sampled burial locations
alt: Area plan and enlarged cemetery grid with sampled burials highlighted and listed.
caption: Unmodified Figure 4 from the 2025 study. The plan identifies sampled graves within the excavated cemetery; it is not a reconstruction of the entire settlement.
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 · unmodified figure; noncommercial use

title: Mehrgarh · a modelled chronology
alt: Bayesian chronological model with nine cemetery phases, probability distributions and a BC axis.
caption: Unmodified Figure 2, model v1.1. Read the probability ranges and phase boundaries together. The revised cemetery chronology does not date the beginning of farming everywhere in the subcontinent.
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 · unmodified figure; noncommercial use

title: Balathal · settlement and excavation
alt: Location inset, exposed settlement walls and archaeologists excavating a stone enclosure.
caption: Published Figure 1. The enclosure includes the context of burial 1997-1, associated with approximately 2000 cal BCE. This specific context falls within the site's longer occupation; it does not date every visible wall.

title: Brahmagiri · looking beneath the surface
alt: Electrical resistivity section with distance, elevation and a colour legend.
caption: Figure 3 from Hill et al. (2026): a modern geophysical model used to investigate a buried ashmound. This is neither an excavated section nor a new date for the Neolithic. The publication year does not change the timeline.

title: Bhimbetka · painted shelter surface
alt: Faded red and dark painted forms on a weathered sandstone shelter wall.
caption: Modern photograph taken in 2022. Bhimbetka's paintings span multiple periods; no exact date is established here for this panel. It illustrates rock-art context, not a securely dated Mesolithic scene.
credit: Yayawar monk, photographed 9 October 2022 / Wikimedia Commons
